summary: Brick light of 1855 at the Mount Hope Bay entrance; discontinued in 1927 (USLHS) or 1928 (nomination), as the Mount Hope Bridge rose overhead. Now a private house that is rented out.

lens.note: Sixth order at first exhibition (NEL); the USLHS record gives fifth order; the Board listed a sixth-order light in 1894; a fifth-order lens from 1902 (NEL). The lens is now removed (USLHS).

structures.note: Two-story square brick tower joined to a one-and-a-half-story brick dwelling (NRHP). The tower was raised six feet and given an iron lantern in 1918 (NRHP) or 1916 (NEL).

access.note: Private residence. The NRHP form marks access as restricted; the USLHS archive lists it as not open to the public.

stay.note: Overnight accommodation offered through Airbnb (NEL, as of 2025).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The USLHS archive gives 1846, and NEL says the Bay State Steamboat Company set up a small beacon that year. The present government light, with its tower and dwelling, dates from 1855 (NRHP; NEL). The 1846 date is the earlier private beacon.

The USLHS archive gives 1927. The NRHP nomination says the lantern was removed in 1928 and that an automatic beacon replaced the light that year; the Lighthouse Service kept that beacon until 1934. Both dates are given in the story.
The NRHP nomination dates the lantern replacement and the six-foot rise to 1918; NEL gives 1916 and says the iron lantern came from the Rondout Lighthouse. Not resolved; both are given.
NEL and the 1894 Board entry say sixth order; the USLHS record says fifth order. NEL says the lens was upgraded to fifth order in 1902. Not resolved.

The USLHS roster gives Sherman 1886 to 1916 and Baldwin 1916 to 1925. NEL gives Sherman 1886 to 1914 and dates Baldwin's start to the early 1920s, but its own log names Keeper Baldwin in June 1915. Not resolved.

notes_for_editor: The NRHP nomination was read in full; the owner's name is in it and is left out of the story (private residence). NEL (New England Lighthouses) is copyrighted: facts are paraphrased, quotations are at most a phrase or a sentence, and its keeper-log entries are second-hand (said to be in the Bristol Historical Society; the original logs were not read). The 1846 beacon rests on NEL and the USLHS year. The USCG Historian's Bristol Ferry page (history.uscg.mil, 1846 and 1855 dates) was refused (403) and its web.archive copy also returned 403, so it is not cited. The Chronicling America search 'Bristol Ferry' gave 58 loose hits, none read or cited. The Bulletin page numbers are PDF pages (11 for 1918, 38 for 1925), confirmed against the form-feed page breaks in the cached PDF text. The 1925 item is in the Bulletin of 1 October 1925. The 1894 Board entry is in the 'lights discontinued' list of the report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1895 (printed p. 11, read from the page header; the volume's index also gives page 11 for discontinuances). The same volume's new-lights list also records the reestablishment on 5 November 1894. The Board gives no reason for it. The 1896 fence item (item 185, Third District) is at printed p. 55 of the report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1896; the volume's index also lists Bristol Ferry at 55. The scan number 63 in the earlier citation could not be confirmed, so the citation now gives the printed page only. The 1855 lens order disagreement (NEL and the 1894 Board list say sixth order; USLHS says fifth) is stated in the story, not resolved. Keeper names come from the USLHS roster (NARA registers via the Kraig Anderson inventory); roster slugs match roster.py output; only Roode is confirmed in a primary record here (Bulletin 1925). The 'Keeper Baldwin' of 28 June 1915 is not linked to Arthur J. Baldwin (1916-1925) because no source connects them. The Bristol depot damage of 1938 and the 1931 depot site are a different property and are not used. The stay correction rests on NEL and on a search result; the Airbnb listing itself was not opened. The current owners are private individuals: the story names no owner and no 1991 buyer; the 1991 buyers' names are omitted here as well.
